content.user_title: Build Responsive React Interfaces With Clear State
content.value_statement: React interfaces can become slow and difficult to maintain when state ownership and asynchronous dependencies are unclear. This skill guides stack-specific decisions with Effect Atom, TanStack Query, and concurrent React patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guide separation of temporary UI state in Effect Atom from server data in TanStack Query.
Identify unnecessary sequential waits and organize independent work with Effect combinators or Promise.all.
Recommend shared mutation scopes for ordered updates and optimistic UI for responsive interactions.
Explain transition, deferred rendering, Suspense, Activity, and effect event usage.
Review component APIs for controlled values, event naming, composition, and visual variants.
Tailor memoization recommendations to React Compiler availability and measured performance.
limitations: Guidance targets repositories based on masseater/typescript-template, not every React architecture.
The source targets React 19.3; verify API availability against your installed release and release channel.
The skill provides documentation, not an executable analyzer, test runner, or performance benchmark.
Source guidance is Japanese and assumes familiarity with Effect Atom, TanStack Query, and Feature-Sliced Design.

use_cases.title: Choose State Ownership
use_cases.description: Plan where form values, shared UI state, server responses, and mutation status belong before building a feature.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers using Effect Atom and TanStack Query

use_cases.title: Review Slow Loader Dependencies
use_cases.description: Identify independent reads, preserve authentication dependencies, and choose Suspense boundaries that keep navigation visible.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Contracts
use_cases.description: Review controlled props, event names, composition patterns, and visual variants for reusable components.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Classify State
prompt_templates.prompt: Use how-to-use-react to classify state for [feature]. Separate temporary UI values, server data, and mutation status. Explain the recommended owner for each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a feature in the supported stack

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Review Component Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component] with how-to-use-react. Check controlled values, event names, boolean props, children composition, and visual variants. List concrete changes.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Remove Sequential Waits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [loader or server function] with how-to-use-react. Identify independent operations and required dependencies. Preserve authorization checks and propose Effect or Promise composition.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reducing latency without changing dependency requirements

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Coordinate Concurrent Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [interactive screen] with how-to-use-react. Address ordered mutations, optimistic feedback, deferred lists, Suspense boundaries, and React Compiler assumptions. Include failure cases and verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Designing responsive interactions with overlapping updates

output_examples.input: Where should search input, fetched results, and save progress live?
output: Keep the current search input in Effect Atom.
Manage fetched results with TanStack Query and query definitions in the API segment.
Use mutation status for save progress instead of maintaining a separate pending flag.
Pass a deferred search value to expensive result rendering when needed.

output_examples.input: Configuration and profile data load sequentially, but only the profile needs the user result.
output: Keep user loading before profile loading because the profile requires the user identifier.
Combine the independent configuration task with the dependent user-to-profile task.
Wait inside the content boundary so navigation does not depend on all data completing.

output_examples.input: Review a dialog that stores its own open state and exposes separate header and footer slots.
output: Expose controlled open and onOpenChange props.
Keep temporary open state in the caller's Effect Atom.
Compose dialog content through children and related components.
Use string props for fixed confirmation text when the dialog content is predetermined.

best_practices: Confirm the repository stack, React API availability, and Compiler configuration before applying the recommendations.
Map asynchronous dependencies before parallelizing work, and keep ordered mutations within a shared scope.
Review state ownership, component contracts, and loading boundaries together when assessing an interactive feature.
anti_patterns: Apply stack-specific restrictions unchanged to repositories built around different state libraries or frameworks.
Parallelize dependent operations or ordered mutations without preserving required execution order.
Copy source examples without checking installed APIs, failure behavior, and application authorization requirements.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides React state ownership, asynchronous dependencies, mutation ordering, concurrent UI behavior, and component API design.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can I use it in any React project?
faq.answer: Its rules target masseater/typescript-template repositories. Adapt them carefully when your project uses different state libraries, frameworks, or conventions.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies or run tests?
faq.answer: The supplied files are documentation. They contain no installation scripts, executable test runner, or automated performance benchmark.

faq.question: Does it require React 19.3?
faq.answer: The source targets React 19.3. Check each recommended API against your installed release and release channel before using it.

faq.question: How does it approach memoization?
faq.answer: It avoids manual memoization when React Compiler is enabled. Otherwise, it recommends lint-guided or measured optimization.
